panels.figure_caption: Facial dysmorphism and other features of subjects with Noonan syndrome heterozygous for mutations in the SOS1 gene. SOS1 mutation-positive subjects generally exhibit typical facial features, including macrocephaly, hypertelorism, ptosis, downslanting palpebral fissures, sparse eyebrows with keratosis pylaris, a short and broad nose with upturned tip, low-set and posteriorly angulated ears, and high forehead commonly associated with bitemporal narrowing and prominent supraorbital ridges. Curly hair is present in most of the patients. Other common features include pectus anomalies (NS10, NS19, NS37), short and/or webbed neck (NS6, NS10, NS19, NS22, NS38), and cubitus valgus (NS37). Keloid scars (NS16), recurrent hemorrhages (NS18), and deep plantar creases (NS38) also occur in these subjects. In some infants, the face is suggestive of cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome due to the coarseness of features (NS39).

Curly hair is present in most of the patients. Other common features include pectus anomalies (NS10, NS19, NS37), short and/or webbed neck (NS6, NS10, NS19, NS22, NS38), and cubitus valgus (NS37). Keloid scars (NS16), recurrent hemorrhages (NS18), and deep plantar creases (NS38) also occur in these subjects. In some infants, the face is suggestive of cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome due to the coarseness of features (NS39).

panels.rationale: Single-panel echocardiogram (parasternal long axis) from an adult patient with Noonan syndrome, supported by the disease-focused article title ('Fatal heart failure ... in an adult patient with Noonan syndrome'). The caption documents enlargement of the right-side heart and thickening of the mitral valve leaflets, and the in-text adds displacement of the ventricular septal wall across Figs. 2-6. The septal abnormality is mapped to the closest vocabulary echo finding (asymmetric septal hypertrophy); the caption-specified right heart enlargement and mitral valve leaflet thickening are absent from the vocabulary and recorded as proposed findings. The presentation is a less common Noonan cardiac phenotype (variant) dominated by right-sided enlargement and late-onset mitral disease rather than classic dysplastic pulmonary valve stenosis.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Hematoxylin-Eosin histology of the resected ventricular septum from a child with Noonan syndrome and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (septal myectomy specimen). The visible myocyte hypertrophy with intricate (disarranged) architecture is the classic histopathology of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, a well-established cardiac manifestation of Noonan syndrome; disease attribution is supported by the article title and caption. B: Azan-stained histology from the same Noonan syndrome patient (septal myectomy specimen) showing blue-stained collagen fibrosis between myocardial cells and a thickened, dense endocardial fibroelastosis layer, matching the caption. Myocardial fibrosis is a recognized hypertrophic cardiomyopathy feature and endocardial fibroelastosis is a less-common highlighted manifestation; these histologic features are absent from the configured vocabulary and are therefore captured as proposed findings rather than assigned finding keys.
